card.name: Chutney
card.tagline: Indo-Caribbean dance — Trinidad's Indian indentured-labour descendants' Bhojpuri folk meets Caribbean wining, hips and hands telling the diaspora story.
card.profile: Chutney is the music and dance genre of Indo-Caribbean communities — particularly Trinidad and Tobago, Guyana, and Suriname — descended from the more than 500,000 South Asian indentured labourers brought by the British between 1838 and 1917. The dance combines Bhojpuri-Indian folk movements (hand mudras, hip rolls, ankle-bell footwork) with Caribbean wining, performed to chutney music's distinctive fusion of dholak/dhantal Indian percussion, harmonium, and modern soca rhythms. Major artists like Sundar Popo, Drupatee Ramgoonai, and Ravi B made chutney one of Trinidad's most distinctive genres, and the annual Chutney Soca Monarch competition is a defining moment of Trinidad Carnival season.
card.insight: Chutney's most controversial moment in Trinidad came in 1988 when Drupatee Ramgoonai — the first major female chutney star — released 'Lick Down Mih Nani,' an Indian-Caribbean number that scandalised the conservative Indo-Trinidadian community by openly celebrating the wining dance vocabulary. Drupatee's defiant success cleared the way for chutney's mainstream acceptance, and today the genre is a defining marker of Indo-Caribbean identity from Port of Spain to Queens, New York.
